title: Push Multicast: A Speculative and Coherent Interconnect for Mitigating Manycore CPU Communication Bottleneck
problem: In manycore processors running parallel workloads, multiple cores repeatedly fetch the same shared cacheline at different times, consuming redundant LLC and NoC bandwidth through independent demand requests. The reactive cache hierarchy does not exploit temporal redundancy in same-data accesses across cores.
method: Push Multicast transforms the LLC into a proactive agent: when it services a demand request, it simultaneously pushes the data to other predicted sharers via multicast, amortizing the bandwidth cost of same-data deliveries. A coherent in-network filter is installed in routers to prune outstanding demand requests that match an in-flight push, preventing redundant traffic. A dynamic pause/resume mechanism adaptively disables pushing when contention is detected, avoiding interference between push-traffic and normal demand traffic.

title: Secondary-Power-Cell-Aware Detailed Placement in Multiple Power Domain Designs
problem: Cross-domain cells in multi-power-domain designs require secondary power routing that competes with signal routing; strict IR drop constraints at advanced nodes make placement for efficient secondary PDN difficult.
method: Integer linear programming (ILP) model for detailed placement accounting for secondary power routing; targeted adjustments to cross-domain cell placement; validated against commercial tools.

title: Bishop: Sparsified Bundling Spiking Transformers on Heterogeneous Cores with Error-constrained Pruning
problem: Spiking transformers combine attention mechanisms with spike-based computation, but their large size and high spatiotemporal volume of computation make efficient hardware acceleration difficult due to variable activation sparsity and the inefficiency of treating attention's binary spike operations with conventional accelerator designs.
method: Bishop introduces the Token-Time Bundle (TTB) container that groups spike data across tokens and time steps for efficient packing. A heterogeneous accelerator routes high-density TTBs to a dense core array and low-density TTBs to a sparse core array via a stratifier. BSA (Bundle Sparsity-Aware) training improves structured TTB-level firing sparsity. ECP (Error-Constrained TTB Pruning) trims spiking query/key/value activations with a provable error bound before and after attention map computation. A reconfigurable TTB spiking attention core executes attention as AND-and-Accumulate operations on binary spikes.

title: MeHyper: Accelerating Hypergraph Neural Networks by Exploring Implicit Dataflows
problem: Hypergraph Neural Networks (HGNNs) based on hyperedge-centric dataflow independently process vertex and hyperedge aggregation tasks, causing significant computational redundancy from recalculating shared information (intermediate feature values) across these tasks.
method: MeHyper introduces a microedge concept that captures fine-grained shared information between aggregation tasks, replacing the hyperedge-centric model with a microedge-centric dataflow that processes shared information once and distributes it to all dependent tasks. The execution follows a Read-Process-Activate-Generate model optimized for parallel microedge task processing. The hardware accelerator features a decoupled pipeline for improved computational parallelism and a hierarchical feature management strategy that partitions on-chip memory across feature granularities to reduce off-chip DRAM accesses for the large intermediate feature vectors generated during microedge aggregation.

title: Treelet Accelerated Ray Tracing on GPUs
problem: GPU ray tracing suffers from poor memory access locality because rays traverse a BVH tree in divergent order, causing excessive DRAM traffic; while treelet-based traversal (grouping BVH subtrees and batching rays per treelet) reduces memory traffic on specialized accelerators, applying it to GPUs is non-trivial and naive implementations are ineffective.
method: The paper proposes Virtualized Treelet Queues with two main components. First, ray virtualization terminates raygen shaders after issuing their trace-ray instruction to free CUDA cores, increasing the number of rays concurrently in flight and enabling more cache reuse within treelets. Second, a dynamic treelet queue architecture switches between traversal modes (intra-treelet vs. inter-treelet) at runtime to maximize efficiency. Additionally, warp repacking is applied to the RT unit to improve SIMT efficiency during treelet traversal.

title: Comparison-Free Bit-Stream Generation for Cost-Efficient Unary Computing
problem: Converting binary radix data to unary representation via comparator-based generators incurs high area and power cost, especially as input count and precision increase.
method: Proposes low-cost comparison-free unary number generation mechanism avoiding comparators entirely. Introduces serial and two parallel (exact and approximate) unary generator designs using alternative conversion logic.

title: Single-Address-Space FaaS with Jord
problem: Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) systems incur millisecond-level overheads from isolating functions in separate address spaces (containers or microVMs), preventing them from meeting microsecond-scale service-level objectives (SLOs) required by microservice workloads. The address-space isolation mechanism forces costly context switches, copy-on-write, and cross-function data copies.
method: Jord co-locates functions in a single address space using hardware/software co-design for user-level in-process memory isolation that extends traditional virtual memory capabilities. Memory isolation and protection are enforced at nanosecond granularity without kernel involvement by leveraging hardware memory protection keys or equivalent mechanisms, enabling zero-copy cross-function communication. Scalable function dispatch is achieved through user-level scheduling that avoids OS-level context switches, allowing Jord to meet microsecond SLOs.

title: DeepPUFSCA: Deep learning for Physical Unclonable Function attack based on Side Channel Analysis support
problem: Physical Unclonable Functions are vulnerable to combined challenge-response and side-channel attacks, but existing machine learning attack methods do not simultaneously leverage both information sources, missing attack opportunities.
method: DeepPUFSCA combines challenge and side-channel power consumption information features during deep learning model training to attack arbiter PUFs implemented on FPGA, demonstrating that fused multi-modal information significantly amplifies attack effectiveness.

title: A PulseWidth-IN-PulseWidth-Out Universal Nonlinear Processing Element for Time-Domain In-Memory Computing Systems
problem: Time-domain in-memory computing lacks efficient nonlinear operators; frequent cross-domain data transmission (analog-to-digital-to-analog) degrades energy efficiency in edge AI systems.
method: PIPO-UNPE: pulse-width IN/OUT universal nonlinear element implementing RRAM-based two-layer ReLU network in time domain; Dynamic Loss-Responsive Subset Enhancement (DLRSE) algorithm for improved function approximation; pulse-driven programmable current source; low-latency dispersion comparator VTC.

title: ANSMET: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search with Near-Memory Processing and Hybrid Early Termination
problem: Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) over large high-dimensional vector databases is both highly memory-bound and computationally wasteful: a large fraction of fetched vectors and their distance computations are ultimately discarded because many candidate vectors are far from the query. This dual inefficiency — excess memory traffic and low data utilization — limits throughput and energy efficiency on general-purpose computing platforms.
method: ANSMET co-designs a near-data processing (NDP) architecture at the memory rank level with a hybrid partial-dimension/bit early termination strategy. Distance calculation and comparison for ANNS are offloaded to near-data units within memory ranks, eliminating main memory bandwidth consumption for rejected vectors. As a vector is streamed from memory, ANSMET conservatively estimates a lower-bound distance using partial dimensions and/or partial bits of each element; if this lower bound already exceeds a threshold, the fetch and computation are terminated early. Data layout within a single memory access and across multiple memory ranks is co-optimized to match the early termination granularity, and a lightweight host-NDP coordination protocol manages index traversal and result sorting.

title: MagiCache: A Virtual In-Cache Computing Engine
problem: Array-level in-cache computing architectures dedicate entire cache arrays as compute arrays, leaving most computing lines idle at runtime while the non-computing arrays absorb large bursty memory accesses—both causing severe on-chip capacity loss and high data movement latency for data-parallel applications.
method: MagiCache introduces cacheline-level in-cache computing: each cache array can dynamically configure individual rows as either computing lines or cachelines with negligible hardware overhead. A virtual engine monitors runtime computation and storage requirements and dynamically reallocates rows within each array between compute and cache roles via cacheline-level space management. An instruction chaining technique enables asynchronous execution of computing arrays, overlapping bursty HBM/DRAM access latency with ongoing computation through pipelined, out-of-order scheduling of memory requests and compute operations.

title: MoE-Lightning: High-Throughput MoE Inference on Memory-constrained GPUs
problem: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs have very large total parameter counts that exceed the VRAM of commodity GPUs, forcing weight offloading to CPU memory or NVMe, which creates severe I/O bottlenecks and low GPU utilization during batch inference.
method: MoE-Lightning introduces CGOPipe (CPU-GPU-I/O Pipelining) with paged weight management: expert weights are stored in pages that are streamed between CPU memory and GPU memory in a pipeline overlapping expert computation with prefetching of the next expert's weights. A Hierarchical Roofline Model (HRM) performance model guides policy selection by predicting throughput as a function of batch size, GPU memory, CPU memory, and I/O bandwidth. The system supports multi-GPU configurations for even larger models (Mixtral 8x22B, DBRX) on 2-4 T4 GPUs.

title: Buffalo: Enabling Large-Scale GNN Training via Memory-Efficient Bucketization
problem: Training GNNs on large graphs using partitioning strategies causes a memory explosion problem driven by the long-tail degree distribution of graph nodes, and suffers from expensive graph partitioning, difficult memory estimation per partition, and slow data preparation (block generation).
method: Buffalo introduces node bucketization: a flexible mapping between nodes and partitions that addresses memory explosion by allowing nodes to be distributed to non-contiguous buckets based on degree, preventing any single partition from holding too many high-degree nodes. Fast graph partitioning is implemented based on node bucketing without requiring expensive global partitioning algorithms. A lightweight analytical model estimates memory consumption per partition before allocation, and graph sampling reduces block generation time during data preparation. Evaluation covers real-world billion-scale GNN datasets.

title: Machine Learning-Driven STL Generation for Enhancing Functional Safety of E/E Systems
problem: Traditional functional safety testing methods like ATPG and BIST are intrusive, requiring additional hardware and disrupting normal operations, making them unsuitable for in-field testing in safety-critical systems.
method: Proposes ML-driven automated Self-Test Library (STL) generation using reinforcement learning to create design-specific test patterns for seamless in-field testing during idle periods. The RL agent learns to generate effective test patterns that avoid operation disruption while maintaining high fault coverage.

title: SkyByte: Architecting an Efficient Memory-Semantic CXL-based SSD with OS and Hardware Co-design
problem: CXL-based SSDs enable byte-granular memory expansion at low cost, but suffer from long flash access latency, unpredictable garbage collection stalls, and a fundamental mismatch between byte-granular CXL access and page-granular flash I/O that wastes significant bandwidth.
method: SkyByte co-designs the host OS and SSD controller with three mechanisms: (1) opportunistic OS context switches triggered when the processor detects long CXL-SSD access delays, hiding latency via thread-level parallelism; (2) a cacheline-level write log and page-level data cache within SSD controller DRAM that coalesces byte-granular writes and performs data merging at log cleaning time to reduce flash I/O traffic; and (3) adaptive page migration that promotes hot CXL-SSD pages to fast host DRAM based on access frequency. The combination reduces both stall cycles and unnecessary flash I/O amplification.

title: HiPACK: Efficient Sub-8-Bit Direct Convolution with SIMD and Bitwise Management
problem: Sub-8-bit quantized convolutions on ARM SIMD (NEON/SVE) processors suffer from incompatibility because SIMD instructions lack native support for sub-8-bit data widths, requiring unpacking operations that conflict with parallel multiplication and negate the memory savings of quantization.
method: HiPACK introduces a packing-centric direct convolution strategy with four key techniques: (1) decoupling the unpacking phase from multiplication by pre-expanding sub-8-bit data into a packed 8-bit layout before the multiply loop; (2) optimizing caching of intermediate packed data to improve L1/L2 hit rates; (3) determining ideal segmentation of the packed layout to balance register pressure and cache reuse; and (4) a Dual Interleaved Register (DIR) mechanism that interleaves two packed-data streams in alternating SIMD registers to enable full-width SIMD multiplication without scalar fallback paths.
